fact_en:
Who made the steam engine much better and more efficient?

James Watt, a Scottish engineer! He greatly improved the steam engine in the 1760s and 1770s.
fact_bis:
Kinsa ang nagpalambo sa steam engine aron mas episyente kini?

Si James Watt, usa ka Scottish nga inhinyero! Gipalambo niya ang steam engine niadtong 1760s ug 1770s.

findings.note: title_bis "James Watt Steam Engine Pahuwat" for title_en "Watt Improved the Engine": pahuwat is from huwat/hulat = to wait (make someone wait), not pauswag/pagpalambo = to improve. The headline therefore reads "James Watt steam engine, make-wait" — the card's key verb (improved, not invented) is replaced by an unrelated action. The card's own body uses the correct word ("Gipalambo niya ang steam engine niadtong 1760s ug 1770s"), which is the evidence the title is the outlier; a child who reads only the title gets no fact at all from it.

fact_en:
How fast do high-speed trains go?

High-speed trains like the Shinkansen travel really fast at about 300 kilometers per hour!
fact_bis:
Unsa ka paspas ang high-speed nga mga tren?

Ang high-speed nga mga tren sama sa Shinkansen modagan og paspas, mga 300 ka kilometro kada oras!

findings.note: title_bis "Bullet Train Shinkansen 320" states 320 km/h, but the English title carries no number and both the en and bis bodies say ~300 km/h ("mga 300 ka kilometro kada oras"). The Cebuano-only child gets two conflicting speeds for the same fact from one card, and the title — the part scanned first and remembered — is the wrong one. Number invented/changed in translation; en title is just "Bullet Trains' Speed".

fact_en: Reflection is when light bounces back off a surface, like a shiny mirror!
fact_bis: Ang reflection mao ang pagbalik sa kahayag gikan sa usa ka surface sama sa samin!

findings.note: title_bis "Pamalandong sa Hayag" for title_en "Light Reflection". In Cebuano pamalandong = meditation/contemplation (root landong = shadow/shade), never optical reflection; a child reading the title alone gets "meditating on light" or "shadowing of light" - the opposite of light bouncing off a surface. The card's own body uses the correct concept ("Ang reflection mao ang pagbalik sa kahayag gikan sa usa ka surface sama sa samin") and never uses pamalandong, which is the outlier evidence that the title is the defect. Correct options: Repleksyon sa Kahayag, or Pagbanaag sa Kahayag. Corpus check: pamalandong occurs in the Cebuano corpus only in the ponder sense ("mipamalandong si Junrey").

fact_en: The Stanley Classic vacuum bottle keeps liquids hot using a vacuum layer between its walls to block heat conduction!
fact_bis: Gipainit sa Stanley Classic vacuum bottle ang mga likido gamit ang vacuum layer taliwala sa mga bungbong niini aron pugngan ang heat conduction!

findings.note: EN: "The Stanley Classic vacuum bottle KEEPS liquids hot using a vacuum layer between its walls to block heat conduction". BIS: "GIPAINIT sa Stanley Classic vacuum bottle ang mga likido gamit ang vacuum layer..." — gipainit = heats/makes hot, i.e. the bottle is described as heating the liquid rather than keeping already-hot liquid hot (gipabiling init). Nothing in the card corrects it, so a child concludes a vacuum flask heats drinks via its vacuum layer, which is physically false.

fact_en: Sitting near a campfire warms your skin! The burning wood emits infrared radiation that travels through the air to reach you.
fact_bis: Mokusog ang panit nimo kung maglingkod duol sa campfire! Ang nasunog nga kahoy nagpagawas og infrared radiation nga moagi sa hangin.

findings.note: EN: "Sitting near a campfire warms your skin!" BIS: "Mokusog ang panit nimo kung maglingkod duol sa campfire!" — mokusog = becomes STRONG/intensifies, not moinit (warms). The remaining sentence only says the wood emits infrared radiation that passes through the air (it also drops "to reach you"), so the card never states that the fire warms you. A child reads that a campfire makes their skin strong — false, and the actual heat-radiation-warms-you point is unrecoverable.

fact_en:
Want to make your hair stand up using science?

You can generate static electricity just by rubbing a balloon to transfer electrons!
fact_bis:
Gusto ba nimo patindoga ang imong buhok gamit ang science?

Makagama ka og static electricity pinaagi ra sa pag-uyog og balloon aron ma-transfer ang mga electron!

findings.note: EN: "generate static electricity just by rubbing a balloon to transfer electrons". BIS: "Makagama ka og static electricity pinaagi ra sa pag-uyog og balloon aron ma-transfer ang mga electron!" — uyog means TO SHAKE in Cebuano (rub = kuskos). Shaking a balloon does not transfer electrons or charge hair; the card teaches a method that does not work. Nothing else in the card (title "Static Elektrisidad", question about making hair stand up) restores the rubbing action, so the fact is unrecoverable from the Cebuano.

fact_en:
Why is a wet banana leaf so slippery?

Its smooth, waxy surface reduces friction! This makes it super slippery when it gets wet.
fact_bis:
Nganong maligid kaayo ang nabasa nga dahon sa saging?

Ang hapsay ug mamantika nga nawong niini nagpakunhod sa friction! Mao nga maligid kaayo kini kung mabasa.

findings.note: "Slippery" is rendered as maligid (= to ROLL / be rolled) in BOTH the question and the conclusion, and nothing on the card corrects it: "Nganong maligid kaayo ang nabasa nga dahon sa saging? ... Mao nga maligid kaayo kini kung mabasa." Title ("Dahon sa Saging") drops the property entirely. A Cebuano-only child is told a wet banana leaf ROLLS a lot -- a different, false claim -- and never learns it is slippery; the surviving "nagpakunhod sa friction" gives the cause but not the observable fact the card is about. Corpus evidence this is an outlier, not regional usage: madulas is used for slippery 70x across the sweep batches, madanglog/maligid never -- every other maligid in the corpus means rolling ("maligid sa lamesa", "maligid lang kini sa ehe", "maligid sa kabayo ang bug-at nga karga"). Note ffct-27102 pairs "madulas ug maligid" for "slipping and sliding", which is fine; this card is the one where maligid stands alone for slippery.

fact_en:
Can a simple iron nail become a magnet?

Yes! Wrapping it with wire and passing an electric current aligns its magnetic domains, temporarily turning it into a magnet!
fact_bis:
Mahimo bang mahimong magnet ang pako nga puthaw?

Oo! Kung ibalot nimo kini og wire ug mo-agi ang electric current, mo-align ang magnetic domains niini, mao nga temporaryo kini nga mahimong magnet!

findings.note: EN "a simple iron nail" -> BIS "ang pako nga puthaw". In Cebuano pako = WING (same batch, ffct-27241, correctly uses "ang mga pako niini" for a paper airplane's wings); Cebuano for nail is LANSANG, which is what the rest of the corpus uses for exactly this experiment (ffct-22579 "paglukot ug kawad sa lansang", ffct-24053, ffct-26540, ffct-13172). The card never says lansang anywhere, so the only object a child is given is an "iron wing" to wrap with wire - the whole hands-on fact (wrap wire around a NAIL to make an electromagnet) is unrecoverable from the Cebuano.

fact_en: The Venus flytrap stores chemical energy in its leaves! When you touch its sensitive trigger hairs, it quickly changes into kinetic energy to snap shut.
fact_bis: Ang Venus flytrap nagtipig ug chemical energy sa iyang mga dahon! Kung mahipos ang sensitive trigger hairs niini, dali kaayo kining mo-convert ngadto sa kinetic energy.

findings.note: EN "When you touch its sensitive trigger hairs, it quickly changes into kinetic energy to snap shut" -> BIS "Kung MAHIPOS ang sensitive trigger hairs niini, dali kaayo kining mo-convert ngadto sa kinetic energy." Hipos = to put away / tidy / gather (corpus ffct-08734 "gihipos... ang liso" = collected the seeds); touch is hikap/tandog. The trigger condition is replaced by a nonsense one and the BIS also drops "to snap shut", so nothing in the card restores what actually makes the trap close - a child cannot answer what triggers the Venus flytrap.

fact_en: A fully drawn bow stores about 50 joules of elastic potential energy! This transfers to the arrow as kinetic energy when released.
fact_bis: Kung hingpit nga gihuyop ang bow, nagtipig kini ug mga 50 joules nga elastic potential energy! Mo-transfer kini sa arrow isip kinetic energy inig buhian.

findings.note: EN "A fully drawn bow stores about 50 joules of elastic potential energy" -> BIS "Kung hingpit nga GIHUYOP ang bow...". Huyop = TO BLOW throughout the corpus (95 hits, all blowing/wind: ffct-05080 elephant blowing air, ffct-16287 wind blowing). Nothing in the card says the bow is pulled or bent, so the stated condition for storing the elastic energy is a false one (blowing a bow). Compare ffct-24843, which states the same physics correctly: "Ang pana nga kawayan MOBALUKTOT aron magtipig og elastic potential energy".

fact_en:
Why are the rocks on the Mayon Volcano trail rough?

The rough volcanic rocks increase friction to help climbers avoid slipping while hiking!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga garbo ang mga bato sa trail sa Mayon Volcano?

Ang garbong nga volcanic rocks naghatag og friction aron dili madulas ang mga nag-hike!

findings.note: EN "Why are the rocks on the Mayon Volcano trail rough? The rough volcanic rocks increase friction..." -> BIS "Ngano nga GARBO ang mga bato... Ang GARBONG nga volcanic rocks...". Cebuano garbo = PRIDE/elegance (corpus ffct-05090: "Garbo sa Palawan ang tandikan" = Palawan is proud of the tandikan); rough is gaspang/magaspang (corpus ffct-04122 "gaspang ang panit sa pagi", ffct-28006 title "Magaspang Kennon Road"). The wrong word is used in BOTH the question and the answer, so roughness - the property that causes the friction - is never stated; the child is asked why rocks are "proud" and cannot answer the card's own question.

fact_en:
Did you know a galloping horse pulling a kalesa has special energy?

Yes! As it moves through Vigan's cobblestone streets, it possesses kinetic energy due to its motion!
fact_bis:
Nahibaw-an ba nimo nga ang kabayo nga nagdagan ug naggukod sa kalesa adunay espesyal nga energy?

Oo! Samtang naglihok kini sa mga bato-batong kalsada sa Vigan, adunay kini kinetic energy tungod sa iyang paglihok!

findings.note: "ang kabayo nga nagdagan ug NAGGUKOD sa kalesa" for "a galloping horse PULLING a kalesa". gukod = to chase; pulling/hauling is guyod or bira. This reverses the relationship — the horse is now running after the kalesa instead of drawing it — and nothing in the card corrects it. Same wrong verb as ffct-27438, so it is a repeated swap rather than a one-off typo.
